product: Automated test equipment and advanced robotics. Semiconductor Test ships the UltraFLEXplus platform with new ultra-high-vector-memory UltraPin5000-EM digital, UltraPort-PCIe6 and UltraVS64-HP instruments for AI and data-center devices, plus the Iris 100 for microLED. Robotics covers Universal Robots cobots and Mobile Industrial Robots autonomous mobile robots.
demand: AI-led and broad. Management cites robust AI-related demand in the Q3 2026 guidance and expects rapid wafer-fab-equipment investment to set up growth in 2027. Q2 2026 saw record Memory revenue on DRAM strength and a NAND final-test resurgence, with stated opportunities in custom silicon, co-packaged optics and hyperscaler programs; Robotics grew sequentially through Q4 2025.
pricing_power: Not found. No price increases are disclosed; growth is described as demand, volume and mix driven. Gross margin is stable near 58 to 59 percent, with FY2026 consensus gross margin around 59.45 percent. The 19 percent single-customer and 44 percent top-five concentration give large buyers leverage over prices and contract terms.
competition: Advantest is the primary semiconductor automated test rival, with additional competition in robotics cobots and AMRs and in product test. Teradyne claims the UltraPin5000-EM offers up to 80 times more vector memory than other market offerings and positions UltraFLEXplus across the full AI device supply chain, from first wafer probe to final rack validation.
team: Chief Executive Officer Greg Smith, who describes the strategy as capturing test and robotics opportunities from wafer to AI data center. A quarterly dividend of $0.13 per share was declared 2026-08-24 and a $1.0B five-year senior secured revolver with PNC Bank as administrative agent was signed 2026-08-07, indicating a conservative balance sheet. No management changes found in the last 90 days.
market_strategy: Sell across the entire AI device supply chain, wafer to data center, by stacking new UltraFLEXplus instruments, microLED test and memory coverage on partnerships with Tokyo Electron on 2026-06-08 and GSME on 2026-09-22, geographic expansion such as the India office on 2026-09-15, and a third leg in Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots automation.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $1,329M rose 104% y/y, above guidance, on AI, DRAM and NAND test demand; six dated raises in 90 days (UBS 440->500, GS 350->465) and new UltraFLEXplus AI instruments.
bear: Q3 guidance $1,200-1,300M implies sequential decline; gross margin slipped 1.1pt to 59.8%; top-five customers 44% of revenue, one at 19%; Baird cut to Neutral 2026-08-21; ~42x forward multiple.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-27 showing revenue below $1,200M or Semiconductor Test down sequentially, proving the AI and memory order cycle has rolled over.
web_what_changed: Since 2026-06-27: Q2 2026 results on 2026-07-28 showed record revenue of $1,329M, up 104 percent year over year, with Q3 guidance of $1,200-1,300M; a $1.0B five-year secured revolving credit facility was signed 2026-08-07; UltraFLEXplus AI instruments launched 2026-09-01; India office opened 2026-09-15; Iris 100 microLED test system 2026-09-21; GSME test-center partnership 2026-09-22.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company news dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was found on the investor relations press release page or in SEC filings; the only dated item today is the quarterly dividend of $0.13 per share payable 2026-09-25 to holders of record 2026-09-04.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, not price. Q2 2026 revenue of $1,329M rose 104 percent year over year and exceeded the high end of guidance, split $1,122M Semiconductor Test, $107M Product Test, $100M Robotics. Management credits AI-related unit demand, record Memory from DRAM strength and a NAND final-test resurgence, and share gains; no price increases were disclosed.
web_suppliers: Diversified but partly single-sourced. The FY2025 Form 10-K states components come from a wide range of suppliers and contract manufacturers, yet certain items are obtained from sole sources, and delays in obtaining timely delivery of certain components impacted manufacturing and shipment timing. No supplier names or capacity figures were disclosed; Teradyne holds 10 percent of Technoprobe.
web_customers: Highly concentrated. The FY2025 Form 10-K reports the five largest direct customers were 44 percent of 2025 revenue versus 36 percent in 2024 and 32 percent in 2023; two specifying customers drove 12 percent and 10 percent, and one direct Semiconductor Test customer accounted for 19 percent including specified revenue. Customer identities are not disclosed.
web_who_loses: Advantest, the main rival in semiconductor automated test, loses share if Teradyne wins AI, HBM and DRAM test sockets. Cobot and AMR robotics rivals lose as Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots scale. Independent test-engineering service firms lose as turnkey models such as the GSME partnership absorb device evaluation, test program development and pilot production work.
web_contradicting_evidence: Baird cut TER to Neutral from Outperform on 2026-08-21 with a $420 target, below the roughly $446 consensus, and 5 of 16 analysts rate Hold. Robotics is only about $100M of $1,329M quarterly revenue. Customer concentration of 44 percent top-five and 19 percent single-customer, cyclical memory demand, China and Taiwan export-control and tariff risk, and a roughly 42x forward multiple all cut against the bull case.
web_if_management_right: Rising wafer-fab-equipment investment plus robust AI test demand extends growth into 2027 and beyond. Consensus modeling implies revenue growing from about $5.1B in 2026 to about $6.3B in 2027 and EPS from about $9.09 to $11.65, with gross margin near 59 percent, as new UltraFLEXplus instruments, microLED test and memory strength convert into durable share gains.
web_if_management_wrong: The memory and AI order cycle rolls over first. Q3 guidance of $1,200-1,300M already implies a sequential revenue decline, so an AI capex pause or DRAM and NAND digestion would hit Semiconductor Test, about 84 percent of Q2 revenue, leaving a roughly 42x forward multiple and a small Robotics segment unable to cushion results, amplified by customer concentration and China export controls.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Technoprobe for probe cards, in which Teradyne holds 10 percent; Tokyo Electron under the 2026-06-08 joint AI and data-center test solution; and GSME, which will run a dedicated Teradyne-equipped test floor from 2026-09-22. Upstream handler, prober and precision-component suppliers gain; downstream hyperscalers, memory makers and outsource assembly and test houses gain faster time to market.
